In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship between the free‐prostate‐specific antigen (free‐PSA) subfractions and the volume of benign prostatic hyperplasia and prostate cancer.
the study of the association of the free PSA subfractions fPSA‐N and fPSA‐I with the volume of benign and cancerous prostatic tissue.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fPSA‐N, fPSA‐I, fPSA/tPSA, cPSA/tPSa, and hK2/tPSA ratios are associated with volume of total prostate tissue and PCa tissue.
the subfractions of tPSA, cPSA, and fPSA, as well as hK2, are significantly correlated with volumes of total prostatic gland, transition zone, and PCa tissue.
the volume of benign and PCa tissue is associated with tPSA, cPSA, and fPSA‐I, and the volume of PCa tissue is further associated with fPSA‐N and hK2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the volume of benign and cancerous prostatic tissues are associated with different subfractions and isoforms of tPSA and hK2.

the volume of the prostate gland and the volume of the transition zone were significantly correlated with tPSA and hK2, whereas the volume of the PCa tissue was significantly correlated with cPSA, fPSA‐I, and fPSA‐N, and not with tPSA, cPSA, and hK2.

the association of PSA and hK2 subfractions with prostate tissue volumes is not only dependent on the type of prostate tissue (benign versus malignant), but also on the type of subfraction (total versus free PSA and hK‐2) and the volume of prostate tissue under consideration (total prostate gland, transition, or cancer volume).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the volume of PCa tissue is significantly associated with the levels of fPSA‐N, fPSA‐I, and total hK 2, and that these subfractions are significantly associated with the volume of total prostate gland and PCa tissue.

fPSA‐I and fPSA‐N were significantly associated with the volume of total prostate and transition zone tissue. fPSA‐i and fPSA N were significantly associated with total prostate volume, transition zone volume, and PCa volume.
fPSA‐N is a promising marker for the diagnosis of PCa.
